name: Hu Kwang
note: Closest to the water. Loudest in a storm.

name: Prong
note: The floor floods twice a year and the tide is invited in.

name: Kongkang
note: Built on stilts because the survey said so and nobody argued.

name: Rakam
note: Thorny on three sides. The fourth is the door.

name: Makham
note: Sour fruit falls on the roof in March. It is not a fault.

name: Sadao
note: Bitter leaves. No mosquitoes worth mentioning.

name: Yang Na
note: The pool was drawn at twelve metres until a root made the argument.

name: Mafai
note: Fruit grows straight out of the trunk, which children find outrageous.

name: Tabaek
note: Flowers for nine days in April and then behaves for a year.

name: Nonsi
note: Yellow on the ground by six most mornings in May.

name: Krathon
note: Highest fruit on the island and nobody has ever reached it.

name: Lamphu
note: Fireflies, most of April, and the island is named for this tree.

name: Salao
note: Bark comes away in sheets. Guests keep taking pieces home.

name: Pradu
note: Scented for one week after the first rain and then not again.

name: Kan Krao
note: Smells of nothing all day. Then, at dusk, considerably.

name: Chan
note: Slow wood. The doors were cut from a tree that fell in 2009.

name: Chik
note: Smells of nothing until ten at night.

name: Krabao
note: Buttress roots you can stand inside during rain.

name: Phayom
note: White flowers, once a year, and the whole ridge knows about it.

name: Takhian
note: Coolest floor on the island. The staff will tell you why.

name: Sak
note: Leaves the size of a dinner tray. They are used as one.

name: Chaiyaphruek
note: Pink for two weeks. Unbearable, in the best way.

name: Sattaban
note: Highest. Last light on the island.

name: Pip
note: Opens after dark and can be smelled from the path.
